attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"path\": \"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_4/projects/trace-verdict-study/paper_framing.md\", \"content\": \"# Paper Framing — trace-verdict-study\\n\\n> v2.4 — [UPDATED 2026-05-15] 修正 calibration 比值用精确值计算 (~63x ECE, ~150x Brier)；加入完整 calibration 数据 + seed robustness 证据最终整合。\\n\\n## Target Venue\\n- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR submission)\\n- Fallback: EMNLP 2026 Findings\\n- Deadline: ARR May 25, 2026\\n\\n## Core Insight\\n\\nVerdict prediction (pass/fail) is fundamentally a **fault detection** task. The minimal sufficient signal is the **exception event** — a compact, structured diagnostic moment that achieves near-perfect accuracy (Qwen 99.83%, DeepSeek 99.33%, cross-model gap = 0.50pp) regardless of model architecture. In contrast, richer trace representations that require deeper execution reasoning show model-dependent effectiveness: VOTA gap = 14.96pp, no_trace gap = 1.77pp. Information density — not training signal distribution — is the primary bottleneck: even oracle loss masking (label-only) cannot close the 13pp gap between full traces and targeted extraction. The design principle: **extract the highest-specificity diagnostic signal; discard everything else.**\\n\\n## Core Claims (3)\\n\\n### Claim 1: Exception-based fault detection is model-agnostic\\n\\nException summaries alone achieve near-perfect verdict prediction across architecturally distinct models: Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B (99.83%) and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B (99.33%), cross-model gap = 0.50pp (at best checkpoint, gap = 0pp). This contrasts with VOTA (gap = 14.96pp) and no_trace (gap = 1.77pp). Exception events are structurally simple (`[ERROR] type: ... message: ...`) and do not require deep trace reasoning — making them universally extractable.\\n\\n**Supporting evidence:**\\n- `vota_exception_only_seed42_v2`: Qwen 99.83%\\n- `deepseek_exception_only_seed42`: DeepSeek 99.33% (epoch3) / 99.83% (epoch1 best)\\n- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: DeepSeek VOTA 84.45% (gap = 14.96pp)\\n- `deepseek_no_trace_seed42`: DeepSeek no_trace 73.36% (gap = 1.77pp)\\n- `vota_no_ae_seed42`: 99.41% — actual/expected removal 不降，非 trivial string comparison\\n\\n**Seed robustness** [UPDATED 2026-05-15] ✅: Qwen exception_only 3-seed 完全一致，构成本文最强 robustness 证据：\\n\\n| Seed | Accuracy | 95% CI | Errors |\\n|------|----------|--------|--------|\\n| 42 | 99.83% | [99.58, 100] | 2/1190 |\\n| 123 | 99.83% | [99.58, 100] | 2/1190 |\\n| 456 | 99.83% | [99.58, 100] | 2/1190 |\\n\\n3 seeds 错误样本 100% 重叠（id=901, 905, 均为 `check_dict_case` 函数, label=pass → pred=fail）。**Irreducible samples**: 模型已达数据集理论上限，variance = 0。\\n\\n**DeepSeek cross-model**: epoch1 best checkpoint 99.83% 与 Qwen 完全一致（gap = 0pp），进一步确认 exception signal 的 universality。\\n\\n### Claim 2: Information density, not gradient dilution, drives trace compression benefit\\n\\nFull traces help verdict prediction (81.8%, +6.6pp over baseline), but VOTA achieves 99.41% (+24.3pp) — a +17.6pp advantage. Label-only loss ablation (plan_002) quantifies the causal decomposition: **gradient dilution contributes ~26% of the gap** (4.5pp; label-only full_trace = 86.2%), **information overload contributes ~74%** (13.0pp; only trace compression resolves this). Even with oracle loss masking that eliminates gradient dilution, full traces still underperform VOTA by 13pp.\\n\\nCross-model evidence reinforces this: VOTA gap (14.96pp) tracks base model execution reasoning capability (Qwen CRUXEval-I 56.5% vs DeepSeek 39.0%, Δ=17.5pp), suggesting trace utilization effectiveness is bounded by pretraining-derived inductive biases. Exception signal bypasses this bottleneck entirely (gap = 0.50pp).\\n\\n**Supporting evidence:**\\n- `full_trace_label_only_seed42`: 86.2% (gradient dilution fix, +4.5pp over standard full_trace)\\n- `full_trace_seed42_v5`: 81.8% (standard full_trace)\\n- `vota_seed42_v5`: 99.41%\\n- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: 84.45% (VOTA model-dependent)\\n- CRUXEval literature data (Wang et al.)\\n\\n### Claim 3: Two-tier diagnostic hierarchy for verdict prediction\\n\\nComponent ablation reveals verdict-relevant trace information has a strict two-tier hierarchy:\\n- **Tier 1 — diagnostic moment signals**: exception summaries (99.83%) and assertion-point information (99.92%) are individually near-perfect and sufficient for verdict prediction. ### Claim 2: Information density, not gradient dilution, drives trace compression benefit

Full traces help verdict prediction (81.8%, +6.6pp over baseline), but VOTA achieves 99.41% (+24.3pp) — a +17.6pp advantage. Label-only loss ablation (plan_002) quantifies the causal decomposition: **gradient dilution contributes ~26% of the gap** (4.5pp; label-only full_trace = 86.2%), **information overload contributes ~74%** (13.0pp; only trace compression resolves this). Even with oracle loss masking that eliminates gradient dilution, full traces still underperform VOTA by 13pp.

Cross-model evidence reinforces this: VOTA gap (14.96pp) tracks base model execution reasoning capability (Qwen CRUXEval-I 56.5% vs DeepSeek 39.0%, Δ=17.5pp), suggesting trace utilization effectiveness is bounded by pretraining-derived inductive biases. Exception signal bypasses this bottleneck entirely (gap = 0.50pp).

- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: 84.45% (VOTA model-dependent)
- CRUXEval literature data (Wang et al.)

### Claim 3: Two-tier diagnostic hierarchy for verdict prediction

Component ablation reveals verdict-relevant trace information has a strict two-tier hierarchy:
- **Tier 1 — diagnostic moment signals**: exception summaries (99.83%) and assertion-point information (99.92%) are individually near-perfect and sufficient for verdict prediction. These signals are structurally simple and model-agnostic (exception cross-model gap = 0.50pp).
- **Tier 2 — behavioral patterns**: loop compression (85.6%) carries substantial signal but is model-dependent and fully subsumed by Tier 1.

Combining tiers introduces noise rather than helping: exception_only (99.83%) > VOTA full (99.41%), p=0.01. Loop_only ≈ full_trace_label_only (85.6% vs 86.2%) confirms VOTA's loop compression precisely extracts the useful behavioral signal from full traces.

- `vota_loop_only_seed42`: 85.6% (Tier 2 behavioral)
- `full_trace_label_only_seed42`: 86.2% (≈ loop_only, confirming extraction equivalence)
- `deepseek_exception_only_seed42`: 99.33% (Tier 1 cross-model validation)
- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: 84.45% (Tier 1+2 cross-model: Tier 2 introduces model-dependent degradation)

**Design principle**: verdict-optimized traces should extract highest-specificity diagnostic signals; lower-specificity signals are redundant and may introduce noise.

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: Existing trace SFT studies (DCSH, TracePile) evaluate only generative tasks and find limited, model-dependent benefit. No prior work has tested trace SFT on verdict tasks (binary pass/fail), nor identified what trace components drive classification performance.

- **Existing approaches & gaps**: DCSH (EMNLP Findings 2025) tested 5 trace formats on generation tasks, finding that "no single trace representation consistently outperforms others." TracePile (NeurIPS 2025) scaled to 2.6M samples but only evaluated generation. TRACED (ICSE 2024) showed traces help encoder-based classification. All existing trace formats are designed for execution simulation, not fault detection.

- **Our framing**: We reframe verdict prediction as **fault detection** and ask: what is the minimal sufficient diagnostic signal? Through systematic component ablation across two architecturally distinct models, we discover that exception events — compact, structured error summaries — are both necessary and sufficient, achieving near-perfect accuracy (99.5%+ avg) with near-zero cross-model gap. Richer trace representations work only when the base model has sufficient execution reasoning capability, making them unreliable for general deployment.

- **Headline result**: "Exception-based trace SFT achieves 99.83% verdict accuracy on Qwen and 99.33% on DeepSeek (gap = 0.50pp), while the same models show a 14.96pp gap on VOTA traces — demonstrating that fault detection, not trace reasoning, is the robust mechanism for verdict prediction."

## Story Arc

1. **Setup**: Trace SFT for code tasks — promising but inconsistent in prior work (DCSH, TracePile). Unknown whether traces help verdict tasks and what trace design matters.

2. **First result — traces help, compression helps more** (single model): no_trace 75.1% → full_trace 81.8% → VOTA 99.41%. Label-only loss ablation decomposes the gap: 26% gradient dilution, 74% information overload. Compression improves accuracy through higher information density, not just cost savings.

3. **Twist — what component actually drives VOTA?** Component ablation reveals exception_only (99.83%) ≥ full VOTA (99.41%). The "trace reasoning" narrative is wrong — verdict prediction is fault detection. Tier 1 (exceptions + assertion-point) subsumes Tier 2 (loops). Actual/expected removal doesn't hurt (99.41%).

4. **Cross-model stress test — the universal vs the contingent**: Exception_only transfers with near-zero gap (0.50pp), but VOTA degrades by 14.96pp on DeepSeek. The model-agnostic component is precisely the one that doesn't require trace reasoning. CRUXEval reasoning gap (17.5pp) parallels VOTA gap — trace utilization is bounded by pretraining. [UPDATED 2026-05-15] Seed robustness (3-seed variance = 0) + calibration (ECE=0.003) 双重确认 exception signal 的 reliability。

5. **Design principle**: For verdict tasks, identify the highest-specificity diagnostic signal (exception events) and discard everything else. Simpler signals are more robust; complexity tolerance depends on model capability.

\section{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:setup}

\subsection{Task Definition}
\label{sec:task}

We study \emph{verdict prediction}: given a code snippet $c$, a test input $i$, and an expected output $o_{\text{exp}}$, predict whether executing $c$ on $i$ produces $o_{\text{exp}}$.
Let $\mathbf{x} = (c, i, o_{\text{exp}})$ denote the static context and $t$ the full execution trace obtained by running $c(i)$.
Each experimental condition defines a trace preprocessing function $f$ such that the model receives $(\mathbf{x}, f(t))$ and generates a verdict $\hat{y} \in \{\text{pass}, \text{fail}\}$.

We formulate verdict prediction as supervised fine-tuning (SFT) in an instruction-tuned chat format.
The model generates a single token---\texttt{pass} or \texttt{fail}---as its response, which constitutes a single token in both the Qwen and DeepSeek tokenizers used in our experiments.
This setup differs fundamentally from code generation: the output space is $O(1)$, so all task-relevant information must be extracted from the input representation.
The trace preprocessing function $f$ is therefore the primary design variable.

\subsection{Dataset}
\label{sec:dataset}

We use the verdict prediction dataset constructed by \cite{placeholder_WangEMNLP2025} from CRUXEval \citep{placeholder_GuICML2024}, a benchmark of 800 standalone Python functions designed for execution reasoning evaluation.
\cite{placeholder_WangEMNLP2025} paired each function with multiple test cases and collected line-by-line execution traces via a Python tracer, recording every executed line, variable assignment, function call, and exception event.
This produced 5{,}910 labeled examples, each containing the source code, test input, expected output, ground-truth verdict, and full execution trace.

We split the data into 4{,}720 training and 1{,}190 test examples.
The test set is pass-dominant: 71.51\% of samples have verdict \emph{pass}, establishing a majority-class baseline of 71.51\% accuracy.
This class imbalance motivates our use of per-class precision, recall, and F1 alongside overall accuracy.

\subsection{Trace Representations}
\label{sec:vota}

\paragraph{Full trace.}
The raw execution trace records every line execution, variable state, and function call in sequential order.
For models with limited context, traces are tokenized and truncated to fit a 2{,}048-token window.
We apply chat-template-aware truncation that reserves token budget for the verdict label at the sequence end, preventing the label from being right-truncated during tokenization---a failure mode that causes complete training collapse (Appendix~\ref{app:truncation}).

\paragraph{VOTA.}
Variable-Outcome Trace Abstraction (VOTA) extracts three diagnostic components from the full trace:

\begin{enumerate}[itemsep=2pt,parsep=0pt,topsep=4pt]
\item \textbf{Exception summary.}
Structured error events in the format \texttt{[ERROR] type: \textit{ExceptionType} message: \textit{msg}}.
Present only when execution raises an exception; absent for successful runs.

\item \textbf{Assertion point.}
A snapshot of the actual and expected output values: \texttt{[ASSERT] expected: \textit{X} actual: \textit{Y}}.
Captures the diagnostic moment where the execution outcome can be compared against the specification.

\item \textbf{Loop compression.}
A behavioral summary replacing repetitive per-iteration trace lines with iteration count and variable change trends (e.g., \texttt{3 iterations, result grows [2] $\to$ [2,4] $\to$ [2,4,6]}).
\end{enumerate}

VOTA is not a lossy compression of the full trace.
It performs \emph{targeted extraction}: each component isolates a specific diagnostic signal while discarding all intermediate execution state.
Prior trace compression work optimizes for generation fluency by retaining a narrative of execution \citep{placeholder_FerrandoArXiv2025,placeholder_TraceCoderICSE2026}; VOTA instead selects the minimal set of events sufficient for a binary judgment.
Figure~\ref{fig:vota_example} illustrates the transformation.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\fbox{\parbox{0.93\columnwidth}{%
\small
\textbf{Full trace} (excerpt, 847 tokens):\\[2pt]
\texttt{L2: x = [1, 2, 3]}\\
\texttt{L3: result = []}\\
\texttt{L4: for item in x: ~~\# iter 1}\\
\texttt{L5: ~~result.append(item * 2)}\\
\texttt{L4: for item in x: ~~\# iter 2}\\
\texttt{L5: ~~result.append(item * 2)}\\
\texttt{~~\ldots~(14 more lines)}\\[6pt]
\textbf{VOTA} (38 tokens):\\[2pt]
\texttt{[LOOP] L4--5: 3 iters, result}\\
\texttt{~~grows [2] $\to$ [2,4] $\to$ [2,4,6]}\\
\texttt{[ASSERT] expected: [2,4,6]}\\
\texttt{~~~~~~~~ actual: [2,4,6]}\\
\texttt{[No exception]}}}
\caption{Full trace to VOTA transformation. VOTA reduces token count by ${\sim}$20$\times$ while retaining only signals relevant to the pass/fail verdict.}
\label{fig:vota_example}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Experimental Conditions}
\label{sec:conditions}

\paragraph{Conditions.}
We evaluate seven trace conditions on Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct \citep{placeholder_Qwen25Coder} and four on DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct \citep{placeholder_DeepSeekCoder}.
Table~\ref{tab:conditions} lists all conditions.
The first four conditions are shared across both models; the remaining three---component-level ablations and a loss ablation---are evaluated on Qwen only.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{lp{4.9cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{Input to model} \\
\midrule
\texttt{no\_trace} & $\mathbf{x}$ only \\
\texttt{full\_trace} & $\mathbf{x} + t$, truncated to 2048 tokens \\
\texttt{VOTA} & $\mathbf{x} + \text{VOTA}(t)$ \\
\texttt{exception\_only} & $\mathbf{x}$ + exception component \\
\texttt{ae\_only}$^*$ & $\mathbf{x}$ + assertion-point component \\
\texttt{loop\_only}$^*$ & $\mathbf{x}$ + loop compression component \\
\texttt{label\_only\_loss}$^{*\dag}$ & $\mathbf{x} + t$; loss on verdict token only \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Experimental conditions. The first four are evaluated on both Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B; $^*$conditions are Qwen-only. $^\dag$\texttt{label\_only\_loss} uses the same input as \texttt{full\_trace} but restricts the training loss to the verdict token, isolating gradient dilution from information overload.}
\label{tab:conditions}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Training.}
All conditions use identical hyperparameters.
We fine-tune with LoRA \citep{placeholder_HuLoRA2022}: rank 16, $\alpha{=}32$, applied to all linear layers.
Training runs for 3 epochs with learning rate $2{\times}10^{-4}$, per-device batch size 4, and gradient accumulation over 8 steps (effective batch size 32).
Maximum sequence length is 2{,}048 tokens.
Gradient checkpointing is enabled for all runs.
The primary seed is 42; we run two additional seeds (123, 456) for \texttt{exception\_only} to assess robustness of the headline result.

All experiments run on 2$\times$ NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs (96\,GB each) with CUDA 12.8.
Each single-GPU training run completes in approximately 2 hours.

\paragraph{Evaluation.}
We report accuracy with bootstrap 95\% confidence intervals ($B{=}10{,}000$).
Pairwise comparisons use paired bootstrap tests on per-sample predictions.
We additionally report per-class precision, recall, and F1, as well as expected calibration error \citep[ECE;][]{placeholder_NaeiniICML2015} and Brier score to assess prediction confidence.

import argparse
import json
import os

import torch
from datasets import Dataset
from peft import LoraConfig, TaskType
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, set_seed
from trl import SFTConfig, SFTTrainer


def load_data(data_dir: str, condition: str):
    """Load train and test JSONL files for a given condition."""
    def read_jsonl(path):
        data = []
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if line:
                    data.append(json.loads(line))
        return data

    train_path = os.path.join(data_dir, f"{condition}_train.jsonl")
    test_path = os.path.join(data_dir, f"{condition}_test.jsonl")
    return read_jsonl(train_path), read_jsonl(test_path)


def to_chat_text(items: list[dict], tokenizer, max_length: int = 2048) -> list[dict]:
    """Convert data items to chat-formatted text with label-preserving truncation.

    Truncates the input (trace) content instead of the right side of the sequence,
    so the assistant label ("pass"/"fail") is never lost.
    """
    texts = []
    for item in items:
        # Measure token overhead from chat template + label
        overhead_msg = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            [{"role": "user", "content": ""},
             {"role": "assistant", "content": item["output"]}],
            tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=False,
        )
        overhead_len = len(tokenizer(overhead_msg, add_special_tokens=False).input_ids)
        # Truncate input content to fit within budget, preserving label
        budget = max(0, max_length - overhead_len)
        content_ids = tokenizer(item["input"], add_special_tokens=False).input_ids[:budget]
        truncated_input = tokenizer.decode(content_ids, skip_special_tokens=False)
        messages = [
            {"role": "user", "content": truncated_input},
            {"role": "assistant", "content": item["output"]},
        ]
        text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=False)
        texts.append({"text": text})
    return texts


def to_prompt_completion(items: list[dict], tokenizer) -> list[dict]:
    """Convert data items to prompt-completion format for completion-only loss."""
    results = []
    for item in items:
        messages = [
            {"role": "user", "content": item["input"]},
        ]
        prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True
        )
        results.append({"prompt": prompt, "completion": item["output"]})
    return results


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="LoRA SFT training for trace-verdict classification.")
    parser.add_argument("--condition", required=True, choices=["no_trace", "vota", "full_trace", "vota_no_ae", "ae_only", "exception_only", "loop_only"],
                        help="Training condition: no_trace, vota, or full_trace")
    parser.add_argument("--data_dir", default="/root/autodl-tmp/trace-verdict-study-data/",
                        help="Directory containing formatted training data")
    parser.add_argument("--model_path", default="/root/trace-verdict-study/models/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct",
                        help="Path to base model")
    parser.add_argument("--output_dir", default=None,
                        help="Checkpoint output dir (default: /root/autodl-tmp/trace-verdict-study-checkpoints/{condition})")
    parser.add_argument("--gpu", type=int, default=0, help="GPU device number")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42, help="Random seed")
    parser.add_argument("--wandb_project", default="trace-verdict-study", help="W&B project name")
    parser.add_argument("--wandb_run_name", default=None,
                        help="W&B run name (default: {condition}_seed{seed})")
    parser.add_argument("--label_only_loss", action="store_true",
                        help="Only compute loss on completion tokens (mask prompt/trace tokens)")
    parser.add_argument("--max_steps", type=int, default=-1,
                        help="Max training steps (-1 for full training)")
    parser.add_argument("--gradient_checkpointing", action="store_true",
                        help="Enable gradient checkpointing to reduce memory usage")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    suffix = "_label_only" if args.label_only_loss else ""
    if args.output_dir is None:
        args.output_dir = f"/root/autodl-tmp/trace-verdict-study-checkpoints/{args.condition}{suffix}"
    if args.wandb_run_name is None:
        args.wandb_run_name = f"{args.condition}{suffix}_seed{args.seed}"

    os.makedirs(args.output_dir, exist_ok=True)
    set_seed(args.seed)

    if "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES" not in os.environ:
        os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = str(args.gpu)
    os.environ["WANDB_PROJECT"] = args.wandb_project

    print(f"Condition: {args.condition}")
    print(f"Label-only loss: {args.label_only_loss}")
    print(f"Model: {args.model_path}")
    print(f"Output: {args.output_dir}")

    train_data, eval_data = load_data(args.data_dir, args.condition)
    print(f"Train: {len(train_data)}, Eval: {len(eval_data)}")

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
    if tokenizer.pad_token is None:
        tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token

    if args.label_only_loss:
        train_dataset = Dataset.from_list(to_prompt_completion(train_data, tokenizer))
        eval_dataset = Dataset.from_list(to_prompt_completion(eval_data, tokenizer))
        print(f"Using prompt-completion format with completion_only_loss=True")

    else:

        eval_dataset = Dataset.from_list(to_chat_text(eval_data, tokenizer, max_length=2048))
